modules.title: Anatomy figure
modules.describe: Anatomical figures with named parts, drawn from real illustrations (credits in CREDITS.md): figure is skeleton, muscles (front), muscles-back, heart, brain or cell. In prompt, `highlight` tints one part ("name the highlighted bone") and the rest of the drawing goes grey. In respond, the figure is in colour and the user clicks a part; `target` is the right one (score 1, else 0) and is shown on reveal. Parts — skeleton: skull, mandible, clavicle, scapula, sternum, ribs, spine, humerus, radius, ulna, hand, pelvis, femur, patella, tibia, fibula, foot; muscles: sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, deltoid, pectoralis, biceps, brachioradialis, forearm, abdominis, oblique, sartorius, quadriceps, adductors, tibialis, calf; muscles-back: trapezius, deltoid, infraspinatus, latissimus, triceps, gluteus, hamstrings, calf; heart: svc, ivc, aorta, pulmonary, pulmonary-veins, ra, la, rv, lv, tricuspid, mitral; brain: frontal, parietal, occipital, temporal, cerebellum, brainstem; cell: membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, er, golgi, mitochondrion, lysosome, centrosome.

height.description: Height in points (default depends on the figure: 340 to 480)

modules.describe: A map from Pluckk's map library (/maps/<id>.json). In prompt it fills the region `highlight` and/or dots the point `mark`. In respond the user clicks once: a point `target` {lat, lon} scores exp(-km / tolerance_km), where tolerance defaults to 6% of the map's diagonal; a region `target` {region} scores 1 inside, 0 outside. On reveal the target shows (with `label`) beside the click.

highlight.description: Region id to fill, e.g. CN-GD

label.description: Name drawn at the target on reveal

modules.title: Map

modules.describe: Steps through k-means on a small made-up 2-D dataset: the unlabelled data, the starting centroids, then alternating assign steps (points take the nearest centroid's colour; the plane is shaded by territory) and update steps (centroids slide to their cluster's mean, with the total squared distance before and after), until nothing changes. Back / Next / Play controls. Deterministic for a given seed.
modules.title: k-means, step by step
Neural networks, side by side
modules.describe: Runs one short sequence of words through different neural network architectures, all drawn the same way (time left to right, one column per word; depth bottom to top: input, hidden units, output), so they can be told apart by what each can see when a word goes in. Each hidden cell is banded in the colours of the words that sway it. `arch` is the one shown first: feedforward (no links between columns, so each answer comes from the current word alone: no memory), rnn (the hidden state is fed into the next step, so earlier words linger and fade; the last step says how far the first word has faded) or attention (each position looks straight back at every earlier word, weighted by relevance rather than distance). `compare` lists which architectures get a tab; switching tabs stays on the same word. With a one-word `sequence`, feedforward is a plain multilayer perceptron stepped through layer by layer (`layers` 1 to 3). Back / Next / Play controls. The activations and percentages are really computed from a small network with seeded made-up weights; `memory` (0 to 1.2) sets how strongly the RNN's state feeds back. Use it on cards about what a feedforward network, MLP or RNN is, how they differ, hidden state, sequence memory, fading memory over long sequences, or attention.

compare.description: Architectures that get a tab (default: all three; [] for no tabs)

sequence.description: The words fed in, one per step (default: The cat sat on the mat)

layers.description: Hidden layers in the feedforward network

memory.description: How strongly the RNN's state feeds back (0: none, so it behaves like the feedforward network)

modules.describe: Reads text aloud: a recorded pronunciation when `src` (an audio URL) is given, otherwise `text` in `lang` (BCP-47, default zh-CN) with the device's voices. Plays once when shown unless autoplay is false; the button replays it. `label` is the button text (defaults to text).
modules.title: Read aloud
